_comment: T161 AC3 — the confirmation layer for mutating recipes. POLICY IS DATA: the step lists live here, not in confirm_step.py, so adding a deploy target is a reviewed edit to this file rather than a code change. Read docs/DEPLOY-CONFIRM.md before editing.
_why_not_the_harness: The obvious place for this is the harness `ask` permission tier. It does not work: `ask` was probed on 2026-08-02 (T161 AC3) and RE-PROBED on 2026-08-10 — both times the command ran with NO prompt. `ask` is a silent allow under this permission mode, so shipping it would be a gate that reads as protection and withholds nothing. This layer prompts at a real terminal instead — and since T435 (2026-09-24) it first refuses any agent session outright and then asks macOS to verify the device owner, because a terminal alone was answered by an agent (agy, live db-migrate, 2026-09-17).
_single_use_why: Steps that may run once under an agreed root, but whose authorization is consumed upon pass so that subsequent standalone executions must prompt (T541).
_always_confirm_why: These re-prompt EVEN INSIDE an agreed root — the owner's carve-out of 2026-08-10: 'have option to confirm only specific steps like migrations'. ⚠️ THE EXEMPLAR IN THAT SENTENCE IS NO LONGER IN THIS LIST. `db-migrate` was moved into `roots.deploy-all` on 2026-08-16 by the decision recorded below in `_notes.one_yes_is_the_decision` — read it before editing either list, because re-adding `db-migrate` here reverses an owner decision rather than fixing a bug, and `project/scripts/tests/test_confirm_step.py` will fail and say so. This note and that one contradicted each other for 34 days (T407, AgDR-0024); they are now worded to be read together.

steps.deploy: Ship ALL 6 surfaces live: api (edge fns), web, cp, join, job, demo — then write the release record.
steps.deploy-all: Everything `deploy` does, PLUS db-migrate (schema write) and a post-deploy knowledge refresh.
steps.deploy-api: Deploy Supabase edge functions to the live project.
steps.db-migrate: 🔴 WRITE THE LIVE DATABASE SCHEMA. Applies every committed migration not yet in the ledger. Not reversible by re-running.
steps.db-backup: Dump the live database to a local .sql file (writes credentials-adjacent data to disk).
steps.storage-backup: Download all 555 Storage objects to a local directory — private buckets included (applications, blueprints, domain scans, the Upwork corpus), so the output is secret material exactly like the SQL dumps.
steps.db-psql: Open an interactive psql session against the LIVE database.
steps.rotate: 🔴 Rotate live credentials — invalidates the current ones everywhere they are used.
steps.sync-secrets: 🔴 Overwrite deployed secrets from Infisical. An empty source CLOBBERS the live value.
steps.sync-wom7api-secrets: 🔴 Overwrite wom7api's deployed secrets from Infisical.
steps.test: Runs the offline test tier — 1513 checks across 73 suites. Read-only: it ships nothing and touches no live surface, but it BLOCKS the deploy if any blocking suite fails.
steps.goldens: Visual golden check for the homepage sections across 5 viewports. Boots a local dev server (or reuses one on :4321) and tears it down. Blocks the deploy on a pixel regression; ships nothing.
steps.smoke-live: Post-deploy structural check against the DEPLOYED site. Runs after the apps are already public and is NON-blocking — it reports, it cannot un-ship anything.
steps.ensure-cv-bucket: Creates the CV storage bucket if absent. No-op when it exists.
steps.upload-cv: Uploads the CV artefact to the storage bucket.
steps.deploy-function: Deploys the NAMED Supabase edge function(s) to production (`just deploy-function <name> …`, T431). Replaced 26 per-function recipes.
steps.deploy-infra-tf: terraform apply -auto-approve on the Cloudflare stack (DNS, R2, zone settings). No plan review.
steps.cf-apply: terraform apply -auto-approve on the Cloudflare stack. No plan review.
steps.supabase-settings-apply: terraform apply on the live Supabase project settings.
steps.azure-jumphost-apply: terraform apply -auto-approve on the Azure jumphost.
steps.sync-api-secrets: Writes the API Worker's production secrets (wrangler secret put).
steps.sync-cf-secrets: Writes the web app Worker's production secrets (wrangler secret put).
steps.sync-cfworkers-secrets: Writes the wom7func Worker's production secrets (wrangler secret put).
steps.sync-cp-secrets: Writes the CP Worker's production secrets (wrangler secret put).
steps.sync-demo-secrets: Writes the demo Worker's production secrets (wrangler secret put).
steps.sync-job-secrets: Writes the job Worker's production secrets (wrangler secret put).
steps.sync-join-secrets: Writes the join Worker's production secrets (wrangler secret put).
steps.s3-delete-apply: 🔴 DESTRUCTIVE — T458 S3: permanently delete one approved batch of fixture accounts or test orgs (auth users, profiles, roles; or a client row and its org).
steps.s5-merge-apply: 🔴 DESTRUCTIVE — T458 S5: delete the casualuser@gmail.com login after moving its audit rows to aleksei@ (identities, sessions and factors of that login go with it).
steps.resumes-upload-live: Upload the 17 non-public CVs and candidate resumes to the live private Supabase storage bucket.

_notes.coverage_matches_the_chain: 2026-08-16: test, goldens and smoke-live were added to the deploy chain (T224/T222) without being declared here, so the 'one yes covers N chained step(s)' count under-reported. A step in the chain but absent from this list would prompt separately the moment it grew a _confirm.
_notes.ttl_sized_to_the_real_chain: 2026-08-16: raised 900s → 2700s (45 min). 900s was set when the chain was shorter, and it had become the reason `deploy-all` re-asked for EVERY app: consent expired partway and each later step prompted again. Measured on the successful run — the wrangler phase alone spans ~4.5 min (09:13:2 → 09:17:4), and it is preceded by `test` (~180s), `goldens` (~45s), six Astro builds and the Supabase edge-function deploy; T224/T222 added the first two. ⚠️ The TTL is a real protection — consent is bound to time so a stale yes cannot authorise tomorrow's deploy — so this is sized to one full run with headroom, NOT removed. If the chain grows again, measure and resize rather than reaching for a number that never expires.
_notes.one_yes_is_the_decision: SETTLED — owner, 2026-08-16, reaffirmed AFTER the real cause was found: 'one yes from human should be enough here.' `deploy-all` takes a single confirmation covering all 23 chained steps, db-migrate and sync-secrets included. ⚠️ Context a future reader needs, because it changes how to treat this: the first version of this decision was proposed while chasing the WRONG cause — the per-app re-prompts turned out to be the confirm-step probe suite deleting the live consent file, not the policy. That was fixed separately (W0M_CONFIRM_CONSENT). The owner was then offered the chance to put db-migrate and sync-secrets back and declined. So this is a considered choice, not a workaround left behind — do NOT 'restore' them as a fix for something else. What one yes authorises: an irreversible live schema write, and a secret-set push to Supabase (overwrite, not delete). Standalone `just db-migrate` still prompts; db-reset, db-backup, db-psql, rotate, sync-env, sync-wom7api-secrets and crawler-deploy remain in always_confirm.
_notes.agent_refusal_and_touch_id: T435, 2026-09-24. Every step is refused, before any rule below, when an agent harness is in the gate's process ancestry or an agent environment marker is set, and a confirmed prompt is followed by the macOS device-owner dialog (Touch ID). Why: agy held a pty, saw the db-migrate prompt and sent the answer itself on 2026-09-17. Adding a mutating recipe means wiring `_confirm` AND describing it here; `just confirm-test` enumerates every justfile and fails on a deploy-shaped recipe without the gate.
